headline: Four straight losses after a nail-biting collapse in the Bay
morning_brew: I haven't seen a four-game skid like this from the C's in a long time, and watching them cough it up against the Warriors on Sunday night was a punch to the gut. We had our chances to steal that one, but an 88-87 loss is the kind of result that makes you wanna hurl your extra-large Dunks right out the window. It is agonizing to watch a roster with this much talent look so out of sync, but my neighbor Rick is already deep into his umpire-and-official dossier, and he's convinced the league is running a sting operation on us. I'm not ready to put on the tinfoil hat just yet, but if we don't fix this mess soon, I might be the one writing the next chapter of Rick's conspiracy manifesto.

Switching gears to the gridiron, it is officially the Mike Vrabel and Tommy DeVito era for the Patriots. Hearing that the team isn't looking for outside help while we navigate the next few weeks without Drake Maye is a bold move by the front office, and honestly, we are all just holding our breath to see if DeVito can keep the ship from hitting an iceberg. It is a massive ask for any signal-caller to step in mid-season, but at this point, we have to hope the coaching staff has a plan to simplify the scheme, lean on the run, and pray the defense turns into the '85 Bears overnight.

It is a quiet stretch for the rest of the Hub sports scene while the front office stays busy with offseason moves. I saw the news about the Red Sox bringing in Nick Fortes to bolster the catching situation, which is a quiet bit of business that I can get behind as we try to build out a deeper roster for next year. It is not exactly a blockbuster, but in this market, you take the steady upgrades where you can find them and hope they pay off when the snow finally melts and we're back at Fenway.

trend_watch.trend: Tatum and the rest of the starters couldn't buy a bucket in the final minutes against the Warriors.
trend_watch.dans_take: If we keep shrinking when the clock hits two minutes, this season is gonna be shorter than a line at the Registry.

trend_watch.trend: DeVito is officially the starter while the team manages the injury situation under center.
trend_watch.dans_take: The kid has a hell of a challenge, but I am rooting for him to make the skeptics choke on their words.

news_digest.headline: Vrabel: Patriots sticking with DeVito as QB1, not looking for outside help
news_digest.dans_take: Sticking with our own is a hell of a gamble, but I respect the loyalty to the locker room over panic-buying a veteran.
